x: At this point we had Murdoch in the first half-dozen, with Clements, Beaumont and Wood in the early twenties. From here it was obvious we should be placed.
About half-way, Clements managed to open up a gap from Wood and a mile from home had established a lead of two hundred yards, which was never reduced.
In Clements, Lucas, and the younger Herbert, we have three junior runners destined for the highest rank. Beaumont, Wood and Tobin are all likely to show improved performances next year.

Tobin was still our first man, and had lost a few places, as had Lucas and Morrell. Murdoch had gained, so had Clements and Stride. These two were running very strongly and we still hoped there might be a chance of a place.
The course was altered slightly to cut out the brook but Stride's time of 29 mins. 15 secs. is, nevertheless, of the same excellent standard set by Stimpson and Clements in previous years.

100 yards (under 19), handicap: 1st, Mullen; 2nd, Sinton; 3rd, Godfrey, 10.5 secs. 100 yards (under 16) handicap: 1st, Kemp; 2nd, Clements, 10.9 secs. 220 yards handicap: 1st, Kemp (16); 2nd, Mullens (10); 3rd, Lowers (2), 22.7 secs. 880 yards handicap: 1st, Isaac (95); 2nd, R.

The final handicap meeting of the season was held at Tooting Bec on Saturday, September 17th, and although the entry for the 3 miles run was up to standard, the other events on the programme were not too well supported. The final of the 100 yards was a good race and Clements just beat Kemp with Mitchell third.

We made up two heats in the 100 yards Boys (under 16) race and the final was won by Don Clements from Malden. Mike Stearman was present to defend his 880 yards Junior title, but he was beaten by a newcomer to our ranks in Gerry Trower, with Bob Wolton third.
